text:
Jesper Bratt has an eight-game point streak, 10 points in that stretch and 21 in 21 games, and New Jersey has won most of those nights. A sixth-round pick from 2016 who has played all 655 of his games for the Devils, he's driving play as well as anyone on the Devils.

The numbers are loud. With Bratt on the ice at five on five, New Jersey takes 63% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 60% of the shot attempts, 8.5 points better than without him. His 17 assists come from real playmaking: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 94th percentile for setting up shots last season, with 72% of his exits leaving the zone with possession. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 98th percentile for driving play.

If anything, the goals are behind. Four on 6.0 expected is a little unlucky, and our talent range projects about 20 goals and 73 points. The 3.44 points per 60 he's scoring now is above his usual rate, so some of the assist pace will settle, but there's no sign the play underneath is a fluke. Watch the goals: they're the part with room to grow.
